content: The 2016 World Health Organization (WHO) Global Guidelines for the Prevention of Surgical Site Infections (SSI) are evidence-based and represent the first global guidelines of their kind. These guidelines are grounded in systematic reviews and provide additional information to support actions aimed at improving clinical practices. They were developed by international experts following WHO’s Guideline Development Process, with the overarching goal of achieving standardization in surgical infection prevention. Key recommendations from the guidelines include the following: 1. Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (SAP) should be administered within 120 minutes prior to the surgical incision, taking into account the half-life of the antibiotic being used. 2. Adult patients undergoing general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation for surgical procedures should receive 80% inspired oxygen intraoperatively. If feasible, this oxygen concentration should also be maintained during the immediate postoperative period for 2 to 6 hours. 3. Patients with known nasal carriage of Staphylococcus aureus undergoing surgery should be treated with intranasal applications of 2% mupirocin ointment, with or without a combination of chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG) body wash, to reduce the risk of infection. 4. Hair removal in surgical patients should either be avoided entirely or, if absolutely necessary, performed using clippers. Shaving is strongly discouraged at all times, whether preoperatively or in the operating room. 5. Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (SAP) should always be administered before the surgical incision when indicated. 6. Patients should bathe or shower prior to surgery as part of good clinical practice. 7. Either sterile disposable non-woven or sterile reusable woven drapes and surgical gowns can be used during operations to prevent surgical site infections. 8. Wound drains should be removed as soon as clinically indicated to minimize infection risk. 9. Advanced dressings should not be used over standard dressings on primarily closed surgical wounds for the purpose of preventing surgical site infections. These guidelines emphasize evidence-based practices to reduce the risk of surgical site infections and improve patient outcomes.
